content.user_title: Moderate Content with Azure AI Safety
content.value_statement: Teams need reliable moderation for text, images, and custom prohibited terms. This skill shows how to use Azure AI Content Safety from TypeScript with REST SDK patterns.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install the Azure AI Content Safety REST SDK and related authentication packages.
Explains API key and DefaultAzureCredential setup for TypeScript clients.
Provides text and image analysis examples for hate, sexual, violence, and self-harm categories.
Documents custom blocklist creation, updates, deletion, and matching during text analysis.
Includes a moderation helper that returns allow status, flagged categories, severity, and blocklist matches.
Lists REST paths, key SDK types, severity levels, and recommended moderation actions.
limitations: Requires an Azure AI Content Safety resource, endpoint, and valid authentication.
Sends analyzed content or image data to the configured Azure service.
Does not replace human review for borderline, legal, or policy-sensitive moderation decisions.
Examples are TypeScript guidance and must be integrated into an application before use.

use_cases.title: Moderate User Posts
use_cases.description: Add harm category checks before publishing comments, messages, or forum posts.

use_cases.title: Review Uploaded Images
use_cases.description: Analyze image files or blob URLs for safety signals before making them public.

use_cases.title: Manage Prohibited Terms
use_cases.description: Create and apply custom blocklists for domain-specific words, phrases, or policy terms.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to configure an Azure AI Content Safety TypeScript client. Use environment variables for the endpoint and key.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a TypeScript example that analyzes user text for harm categories. Include error handling with isUnexpected and readable result output.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Images
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt my upload flow to analyze an image with Azure AI Content Safety. Explain when to use base64 content or a blob URL.

prompt_templates.title: Build Policy Helper
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reusable moderation helper with severity thresholds and custom blocklists. Return allow status, flagged categories, and blocklist matches.

output_examples.input: A request to moderate a new forum post before publishing.
output_examples.output: The response explains the text analysis call, category selection, severity thresholds, and an allow or review decision.

output_examples.input: A request to screen an uploaded image stored in Azure Blob Storage.
output_examples.output: The response recommends the image analysis endpoint and explains how to use a blob URL for review.

output_examples.input: A request to block company-specific prohibited terms.
output_examples.output: The response outlines blocklist creation, item updates, and matching during text analysis.

best_practices: Keep Azure credentials in environment variables or managed identity, and avoid logging them.
Use conservative severity thresholds for public content and route borderline cases to human review.
Tell users when their content will be sent to Azure for safety analysis.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode Azure keys, endpoints for private tenants, or production blocklist names in source code.
Do not treat severity scores as final legal or policy decisions without review paths.
Do not analyze private files or images unless the user selected them for moderation.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps build TypeScript moderation flows using Azure AI Content Safety for text, images, harm categories, and blocklists.

faq.question: Does it support API key authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to create a REST client with an endpoint and AzureKeyCredential.

faq.question: Can it use managed identity?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes DefaultAzureCredential guidance for Azure environments that support managed identity.

faq.question: Can it moderate images?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers base64 image content and blob URL inputs for image analysis.

faq.question: Does it manage custom blocklists?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents creating, listing, updating, deleting, and applying text blocklists.

faq.question: Is human review still needed?
faq.answer: Yes. Use human review for appeals, ambiguous content, and policy decisions with legal or safety impact.
